ledger.claim: This trip deviates from the route the rider booked. The GPS trace runs 11.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure — 11.18 km, not the rounded 11.2 km convenience copy — the governing measurement.

The rider's complaint is not that a detour happened — the closure explains that — but that the detour cost them ERP they never agreed to. The route they booked carries no ERP at all: trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and the routing engine records the optimal route as 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. Every cent of the $4.00 of ERP on this fare was created by leaving that no-gantry corridor; none of it belongs to the trip the rider booked.

Both charged gantries are itemised in the fare breakdown as lying off the optimal route: CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00, each carrying on_optimal_route false, with the breakdown's own on-optimal-route ERP total at $0.00 and its off-optimal-route total at $4.00. The trace confirms the vehicle actually passed both points (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m). These are genuine off-route pass-through charges for gantries that form no part of the booked route, and they are precisely what the rider contests.

The LTA DataMall closure EV-ADVIS-00103-01 exonerates the distance and time charges under POL-RD-03: it names Braddell Road between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd, its 05:30–12:00 window overlaps the trip, and its geometry intersects the booked optimal route. But exoneration of the driver's conduct does not shift the government-set pass-through onto the rider. Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is exonerated as an external event, off-route ERP is still refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at SGD 12.00 per trip. The rider did not cause the closure any more than the driver did, and the $4.00 of gantry charges they never chose must come back.

The $4.00 is refundable whichever way the closure is treated, so no reading of the record leaves it with the rider. If POL-RD-03 exoneration applies, POL-RD-09(2) returns it as a pass-through correction. If the judge declines to exonerate, POL-RD-09(1) and POL-RD-02 still return it, because a recomputed fare built on the optimal route (16.63) contains ERP for on-optimal-route gantries only — here 0.00 — so the $4.00 is comprehended inside the refund and is never added on top. Either route to the ruling ends with the rider whole on the ERP.

The driver cannot move this ERP to the rider under POL-RD-04, because the chat runs the other way. At 08:12:30 the driver announced 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah'; the rider's only message is 'ok' at 08:12:58 — an acknowledgment of the driver's choice, not a rider instruction. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on, corroborated through chat_message.waypoint_hint; the rider's message carries no waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable on this record, and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund.

The rider has carried the initial POL-RD-08 burden and it has shifted. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00103, and the unimpaired trace shows an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold. To resist, the driver must point to a specific artifact and clause; the only exculpatory artifact on file — the closure advisory — is directed at the distance and time lines, not at the $4.00 of ERP the rider is disputing, and it discharges nothing on those pass-through lines.

The road closure fully exonerates this route under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 (ADV-20260714-031, severity HIGH) closes 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd' from 05:30 to 12:00 on 2026-07-14, and the trace window (first fix 08:07:20, last fix 08:36:20) sits squarely inside that window. The POL-RD-03 cap is min(measured excess 2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km. The whole of the measured excess is therefore justified, nothing is left unexonerated, and the driver keeps the fare computed on the closure-adjusted optimal.

All three POL-RD-03 conditions are met on this record: (a) the advisory names a road the optimal route traverses - the trip_record's own optimal_route_source is 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry', the same Braddell Road the advisory closes; (b) its validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle on that segment (intersects_route true, overlaps_trip_window true, overlap_minutes 35.2); and (c) the driven line leaves the optimal corridor and rejoins it, running 11.18 km against an 8.2 km optimal, crossing two CTE gantries each flagged on_optimal_route false, exactly the 'Diversion via Lorong 1 Toa Payoh or CTE' the advisory describes. The driven 11.18 km is within 0.58 km of the 10.6 km shortest lawful alternative, inside the 1.0 km tolerance built into the POL-RD-03 cap.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 does not run against the rider's benefit. POL-RD-02 is engaged only where a deviation is established AND 'no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'; here the exculpatory clause excuses 100% of the excess. POL-RD-03 directs POL-RD-02 only to the excess BEYOND the cap, and there is none. The driver was not at fault for an emergency water-main closure, so the distance and time charges stand and no distance-based refund is owed to the rider.

The rider's only recovery is the off-route ERP pass-through under POL-RD-09(2): where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03 the distance and time charges stand, but off-route ERP is refunded standalone, capped at SGD 12.00. The off-route ERP actually charged is SGD 4.00 (CTE Braddell Rd SGD 3.00 plus CTE Moulmein Rd SGD 1.00, both on_optimal_route false; off_optimal_route_total 4.00, on_optimal_route_total 0.00). The correction is therefore SGD 4.00 - not the SGD 9.00 contested, and not the SGD 8.50 that an UNadjusted POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked 8.2 km optimal would yield. The closure is worth roughly SGD 4.35 to the driver and that reduction is exactly what POL-RD-03 exists to deliver.

Neither ERP line is a phantom charge, so POL-RD-09(4) adds nothing to the rider's recovery. Under the POL-RD-09 match rule a gantry is treated as crossed where a trace fix lies within 250 m of it: the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry at (1.3401, 103.8496) has a nearest fix at 0.0 m (fix index 33, 08:12:50) and the CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry at (1.324, 103.854) has a nearest fix at 40.25 m (fix index 74, 08:19:40), both well inside the radius, and both charge times (08:14:06 and 08:19:41) fall inside the trace window. There is no unmatched line, no billing-integrity failure, and no ground for a full ERP refund on top of the capped pass-through.

The rider had contemporaneous notice of the diversion and did not object. At 08:12:30 the driver messaged 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' and the rider replied 'ok' at 08:12:58, both read within about 30 seconds; that exchange predates the second gantry charge at 08:19:41. It corroborates that the diversion was the driver's response to the closure, not a route taken against the rider's wishes, and it is consistent with the advisory the platform elsewhere holds.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern and no POL-RD-06 uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 553 - below the 3-flag test and below the 0.05 ratio test - so no pattern is established and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the driver-conduct referral of POL-RD-06 follows. The deviation is in any event not MATERIAL on this trip (36.3% and 2.98 km, both under the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds), so the POL-RD-06 check was not even required. POL-GEN-01 confines any profile use to these named counters; the driver's record is not a ground for an adverse finding.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07, so there is no route to ESCALATE. It carries 175 fixes at a 10.0 s sampling interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0; limbs (a) to (c) are not engaged and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation ground is closed. The excess rests on a clean, unbroken trace and the case can and should be decided on this trip's own evidence rather than held for a human reviewer.

Even on the tribunal's alternative reading the rider's recovery is bounded at SGD 4.15. The driver has discharged the POL-RD-08 shifted burden by pointing to a specific advisory ID (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) and a specific clause (POL-RD-03), so the excess is excused rather than refunded. If the tribunal prefers to run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal of 11.18 km instead, the refund is charged_total 25.12 less recomputed_fare 20.993 = 4.127, rounded up to SGD 4.15 - and that figure already excludes the off-route gantries, so the ERP cannot be counted a second time (POL-RD-09(1)). Either way the rider is far short of the SGD 9.00 contested.

replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00103, weight 1.0, unbroken 175 fixes at 10 s) measures 11.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 8.2 km (EV-TRIP-00103) — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34%. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a route deviation is established on this trip's own trace; it is not a MATERIAL deviation (both figures sit under the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds). The deviation is nevertheless fully exonerated under POL-RD-03. The LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 (weight 1.0) closes Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00, a road the booked optimal route itself uses, and its window overlaps the 08:07–08:36 trip. The POL-RD-03 cap is min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so the whole excess is justified and the distance-time charges stand; POL-RD-02 therefore does not run in either direction, and no distance refund is owed. What the closure does not do is put the CTE gantries on the rider's route. The booked optimal route carries $0.00 of ERP (trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), while the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00103, weight 1.0) itemises $4.00 of off-route ERP — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00, both flagged on_optimal_route false, against an on-optimal-route total of $0.00. Under POL-RD-09(2) those off-route charges are refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction because the rider did not cause the closure either; the $4.00 is well under the $12.00 per-trip cap. Both gantries are genuine crossings — the nearest trace fixes are 0.0 m and 40.25 m away, inside the 250 m match radius — so POL-RD-09(4) yields no phantom-line finding and no billing-integrity referral. The $4.00 is refunded once only: because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the deviation, POL-RD-02 does not also run, so there is no double count under POL-RD-09(1). On the parties' arguments: the rider's claims that the deviation is established and that the $4.00 is off-route ERP are accepted; the driver's claims that the closure exonerates the distance and time lines, that the two gantries are real, and that the rider's only recovery is the capped pass-through are also accepted, and both advocates arrive at the same $4.00 figure under POL-RD-09(2). The rider's claim that POL-RD-04 is unavailable is accepted — the driver's message announced the CTE route and the rider's 'ok' is an acknowledgement, not a rider instruction, and it carries no waypoint_hint, so the clause cannot run and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund. The driver's alternative figure of $4.15 (a POL-RD-02 recomputation against the closure-adjusted 11.18 km optimal) is noted but does not displace the primary route, because POL-RD-03 leaves nothing unexonerated for POL-RD-02 to refund. No repeat-deviation pattern is established (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 553), so POL-RD-06 produces neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a conduct referral; and the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. Confidence rests on artifacts all at weight 1.0, giving a cap of 1.0. Of the $9.00 contested, $4.00 is refunded to the rider and the balance of $5.00 remains payable.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
